title: Tax Years Since Incorporation Calculator | Every Year and Its Due Date
content:
Catch-Up

Tax Years Since Incorporation Calculator

Enter the incorporation date and the first fiscal year-end to list every tax year the corporation has had, each filing date and which returns are now overdue.

Lists every tax yearNames each filing dateCounts what is overdueNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

The incorporation date and the first fiscal year-end

Enter both dates and every tax year since appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Why the Count Matters More Than the Years

A corporation has a tax year for every year it has existed, whether or not it traded, and a T2 is due for each one. The number people usually have in mind is how long ago they incorporated. The number that matters is how many tax years have ended since, because that is how many returns are owed.

The two can differ, and a short first year is why. A corporation incorporated in March 2023 that chose a December 31 year-end had its first tax year end nine months later, in December 2023. By January 2027 it has four tax years behind it — 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and owes four returns, which is one more than the three years it feels like it has been going.

The First Year Is the One That Catches People

A first tax year runs from the date of incorporation to the first year-end chosen, and it may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days. It is almost always shorter than twelve months, and it is still a full tax year needing a full return.

Where the first year-end entered here produces a first year longer than 53 weeks, the year-end on record with the Canada Revenue Agency is probably not the one entered, and a transmission against the wrong year-end is rejected. The 53-week first tax year checker tests that one question on its own.

What an Overdue Year Actually Costs

Each outstanding nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, and several years are transmitted in one sitting rather than one at a time.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

How a Corporation Ends Up With More Tax Years Than It Expects

Four things add a tax year, and all four are common in corporations that were set up and then left alone.

What happenedEffect on the countReturns owed
Incorporated part-way through a yearA short first tax year, then full onesOne for the short year, one for each year after
The fiscal year-end was changedA short stub year at the changeoverOne extra return for the stub period
The corporation was dissolved mid-yearA short final year ending on the dissolution dateOne final return
The corporation amalgamatedEach predecessor’s year ends the day beforeOne final return per predecessor

Each of those is a separate tax year and needs its own return, and each nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. None of them is covered by filing the year on either side of it.

A corporation that holds shares, owns rental property or holds investments is not nil, and in any year it receives something there are figures to report. A Quebec corporation files a CO-17 as a separate return and an Alberta corporation files an AT1 the same way, neither of them covered by the fee here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a Year With No Activity Still Count as a Tax Year?

Yes. A tax year ends on the fiscal year-end whether anything happened in it or not, and a T2 is due for it.

What If I Do Not Know the First Fiscal Year-End?

It is on the first notice of assessment, and it is the year-end the Canada Revenue Agency holds. A transmission against a different year-end is rejected.

Is There a Limit on How Many Years Can Be Filed at Once?

No. Several years are transmitted in one sitting. Each nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Does the Count Include the Year That Has Not Finished?

No. The table lists tax years that have ended, because a return cannot be transmitted until the year is over. The year in progress is named separately with its own date.

Do I Need Bookkeeping for Every One of Those Years?

Not for a year with no transactions. A nil return is built from the corporation’s own position, and whichever schedules that position requires are inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

title: Days Overdue Calculator | How Late a T2 Return Is
content:
Lateness

Days Overdue Calculator

Enter the fiscal year-end to see the filing date, how many calendar days a T2 is overdue and how many business days, counted on the same holiday calendar the deadline uses.

Calendar and business daysApplies the holiday shiftSays what a late nil year costsNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

The fiscal year-end of the return in question

Enter the year-end and the count appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Two Counts, Two Different Numbers

Calendar days and business days are not the same count, and the gap between them widens the longer a return sits. Thirty calendar days is about twenty business days. A year overdue is about 365 calendar days and about 250 business days.

Both are shown because they answer different questions. Calendar days is how long the year has been open. Business days is how much working time has passed, which is the one that matters when a deadline on the other side of the lateness is being worked towards.

The Count Starts From the Shifted Date

The filing date is six months after the fiscal year-end, and where that lands on a weekend or a statutory holiday it moves forward to the next business day. The count here starts from the moved date, not the unmoved one, so a return is never shown as overdue on a day the deadline had not actually passed.

The due date weekend and holiday shift calculator shows that step on its own, and the nil T2 deadline calculator works the whole date out from a year-end.

What Being Late Changes About the Fee

Nothing. A late nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, the same as one filed on time, and it can be transmitted today.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

What Each Stage of Lateness Changes

Lateness is not one state. What is at stake shifts as a year stays open, and the fee for the return itself does not move at any point on this list.

How lateWhat has changedCost of the nil return
Before the filing dateNothing. The return can be transmitted as soon as the year has ended$300.00 plus HST per tax year
Days lateThe year is open. A non-resident-owned corporation is already accruing $25.00 per day$300.00 plus HST per tax year
Months lateThe year stays open, and it blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution$300.00 plus HST per tax year
A demand to file arrivesThe demand sets its own deadline and opens the way to an arbitrary assessment$300.00 plus HST per tax year
100 days late, non-resident-ownedThe per-day charge has reached its $2,500.00 ceiling$300.00 plus HST per tax year
Years lateEvery year is still owed, and the oldest is no closer to closing itself$300.00 plus HST per tax year, for each year outstanding

An unfiled year does not lapse and does not expire. It stays open until the return is filed, which is why the oldest year on the list is usually the one worth starting with.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does an Unfiled Year Ever Expire?

No. The year stays open until the return is filed. There is no point at which an unfiled T2 stops being owed.

Why Are the Two Day Counts Different?

Weekends and the statutory holidays treated as closed days are not business days, so the business-day count is always the smaller of the two.

Is a Late Nil Return More Expensive?

No. It is $300.00 plus HST per tax year whether it is on time or years late.

Should the Oldest Year Be Filed First?

It is the usual order, because the oldest year is the one that has been open longest and the one most likely to have drawn correspondence. Several years are transmitted in one sitting either way.

What If a Demand to File Has Already Arrived?

A demand sets its own deadline, and that deadline is on the letter. Responding to it is a different task from simply filing late, and the guide to responding to a demand sets out the order.

title: Next T2 Due Date Checker | Which Filing Date Comes Next
content:
What Is Next

Next T2 Due Date Checker

Enter any one of the corporation fiscal year-ends to see which T2 filing date comes next, how many business days away it is and whether the return can be transmitted already.

Works from any past year-endNames the next date dueSays whether it can be filed nowNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

Any one of the corporation’s fiscal year-ends

Enter a year-end and the next filing date appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Next Date Due Is Usually the Last Year’s

This is the part that trips people. The next T2 filing date is rarely the one belonging to the year-end coming up. It is almost always the one belonging to the year-end that has already passed, because the six months sits between them.

A corporation with a June 30 year-end, asked in October which date is next, has December 31 next, for the year that ended in June. The following June is not the next filing date, it is the next year-end, and its return is not due until the December after that.

A Return Can Be Filed the Day the Year Ends

Nothing requires waiting for the filing date. A nil T2 can be transmitted as soon as the tax year has ended, and filing it the week the year closes closes the year.

Where the year named here has already ended, the return is ready to go now and the date shown is simply the last day it can go without being late.

One Date at a Time, Not a Schedule

This tool names the next date. The tax years since incorporation calculator lists every year and every date at once, which is the better view where more than one year is outstanding, and the days overdue calculator counts how late a year already is.

The Same Year-End Asked at Four Different Times

The answer depends on when the question is asked, which is why a remembered date goes stale. These four rows are one corporation with a June 30 year-end, asked in four different months.

Asked inNext filing dateFor the year endedCan it be filed today
August 2026December 31, 2026June 30, 2026Yes, that year has ended
October 2026December 31, 2026June 30, 2026Yes, that year has ended
February 2027December 31, 2027June 30, 2027No, that year has not ended
August 2027December 31, 2027June 30, 2027Yes, that year has ended

The February row is the one worth noting. The next filing date is eleven months away, but nothing can be transmitted yet, because the year it belongs to has not finished. The December 2026 date has already gone by, so if that return was not filed it is now overdue rather than upcoming.

Every one of these dates is six months after a fiscal year-end, moved to the next business day where it lands on a weekend or a statutory holiday. A nil return for any of these years is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why Is the Next Date for a Year That Has Already Ended?

Because the six months runs after the year-end. The return for a year that ended in June is due in December, so between July and December the next date due belongs to the year just finished.

Can a Return Be Filed Before the Due Date?

Yes, and for a nil return there is no reason not to. It can be transmitted as soon as the tax year has ended.

What If the Year-End Entered Is From Years Ago?

It still works. Any past year-end establishes the month and day, and the tool steps forward from there to the next date that has not passed.

Does the Date Move for a Weekend or a Holiday?

Yes. Where six months after the year-end lands on a weekend or a statutory holiday, the filing date moves to the next business day.

What If More Than One Year Is Outstanding?

Then the next date is not the useful number. The unfiled years checker lists what is outstanding, and each nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

title: Final T2 Return Due Date Calculator | Dissolution Filing Date
content:
Dissolution

Final T2 Return Due Date Calculator

Enter the last fiscal year-end and the date of dissolution to see the final tax year period, its length and the date the final T2 is due.

Names the final tax yearSix months from dissolutionFlags the short final yearNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

The last fiscal year-end and the date of dissolution

Enter both dates and the final return period appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Dissolution Ends the Tax Year on Its Own Date

A corporation’s last tax year does not run to its usual year-end. It ends on the date of dissolution, and the final T2 covers the period from the day after the previous year-end to that date.

The six months then runs from the dissolution date. A corporation with a December 31 year-end dissolved in March does not file to December and does not get until the following June: it files to the March date and the return is due six months after that.

The Final Year Is Almost Always Short

Unless dissolution happens to fall on the year-end, the final tax year is a short one. A short year is a full tax year for every purpose that matters here: it needs its own return, it gets the same six months, and a nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

The short tax year deadline calculator works out the filing date for any short period on its own.

Every Earlier Year Has to Be In First

The final return is the last one, not the only one. Every earlier tax year still has to be filed, nil years included, and an unfiled year blocks a clearance certificate and blocks the dissolution behind it.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

The dissolution readiness checker runs the whole list, and the clearance certificate requirement checker covers the certificate itself.

The Order the Dates Fall In

Four dates matter on a dissolution, and they do not fall in the order people expect. This is one corporation with a December 31 year-end, dissolved on March 15, 2027.

DateWhat it isWhat is owed
December 31, 2026The last ordinary fiscal year-endA T2 for the year ended that day, due June 30, 2027
January 1, 2027The final tax year beginsNothing yet
March 15, 2027Dissolution, and the final tax year endsA final T2 for January 1 to March 15, due September 15, 2027
September 15, 2027The final T2 filing dateThe last return the corporation ever files

Two returns, not one, and the ordinary year’s return falls due in June, before the final one. Each nil return is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. A corporation that held investments or rental property, or that paid or received a dividend in either period, is not nil for that period.

Distributing property before the final return is settled leaves the person who distributed it personally exposed for amounts the corporation turns out to owe, which is what a clearance certificate is for.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Final Return Go to the Usual Year-End?

No. The tax year ends on the date of dissolution, and the return covers the period to that date.

Is the Final Return Due Sooner Because the Year Was Short?

No. Six months runs from the year-end whatever the length of the period, so a short final year gets the same six months.

How Many Returns Does a Mid-Year Dissolution Mean?

Usually two: the ordinary year that ended before it, and the short final year ending on the dissolution date. Each nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Can a Corporation Dissolve With Years Unfiled?

An unfiled year blocks a clearance certificate and blocks the dissolution. The outstanding years have to be filed first.

Is the Final T2 Different From an Ordinary One?

It is the same return for a shorter period. What changes is the period it covers and the date it is due, not the form or what it costs.

title: Amalgamation T2 Due Date Calculator | Predecessor Final Returns
content:
Amalgamation

Amalgamation T2 Due Date Calculator

Enter a predecessor fiscal year-end and the amalgamation date to see the predecessor final tax year, the date its return is due and when the new corporation first tax year begins.

One final return per predecessorThe year ends the day beforeNames the new first year windowNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

A predecessor’s last fiscal year-end and the amalgamation date

Enter both dates and the periods appear here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Year Ends the Day Before, Not on the Day

An amalgamation ends each predecessor corporation’s tax year on the day before the amalgamation date. The new corporation’s first tax year begins on the amalgamation date itself. The two periods do not overlap and there is no gap between them.

That one-day offset is the whole reason this calculator exists. A final return filed to the amalgamation date is filed to a year-end the Canada Revenue Agency does not hold, and the transmission is rejected for the year-end rather than for anything in the return.

One Final Return for Each Predecessor

Every predecessor files its own final return for its own period. An amalgamation of two corporations means two final returns, an amalgamation of three means three, and each one is a separate filing.

Each predecessor may also have its own year-end, so the periods can be different lengths even though they all end on the same day. Each nil final return is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

The New Corporation Starts Its Own Clock

The corporation that comes out of an amalgamation is a new corporation for tax year purposes, and its first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days from the amalgamation date.

That first year then has its own return, due six months after whichever year-end it chooses inside that window. The 53-week first tax year checker tests a proposed first year-end against the limit.

What Each Corporation Owes and When

Two predecessors with different year-ends, amalgamating on July 1, 2027. Three corporations appear on this list and three sets of obligations come out of it.

CorporationFinal or first tax yearReturn due
Predecessor A, December 31 year-endJanuary 1, 2027 to June 30, 2027December 31, 2027
Predecessor B, March 31 year-endApril 1, 2027 to June 30, 2027December 31, 2027
The amalgamated corporationBegins July 1, 2027, first year-end no later than July 5, 2028Six months after whichever year-end it chooses

Both predecessor years end June 30, 2027, the day before the amalgamation, so both final returns fall due on the same date even though the periods are different lengths. Neither one runs to its own usual year-end.

A predecessor that held shares, owned rental property or paid or received a dividend in its final period is not nil for that period. A Quebec corporation files a CO-17 as a separate return and an Alberta corporation files an AT1 the same way, neither of them covered by the fee here.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the Predecessor File to the Amalgamation Date?

No. The tax year ends the day before the amalgamation date. Filing to the amalgamation date itself is filing to the wrong year-end.

How Many Final Returns Does an Amalgamation Need?

One for each predecessor corporation. Each nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Do the Predecessors Have to Share a Year-End?

No. They can have different year-ends and therefore different period lengths, but all the final periods end on the same day, the day before the amalgamation.

Does the New Corporation Inherit the Old Year-End?

It chooses its own first year-end, and that first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks from the amalgamation date.

Are Earlier Years of a Predecessor Still Owed?

Yes. The final return is the last one, not the only one. Any earlier unfiled year is still owed and is still $300.00 plus HST per tax year for a nil year.

title: Short Tax Year Deadline Calculator | Filing Date for a Stub Period
content:
Short Year

Short Tax Year Deadline Calculator

Enter the first and last day of a short tax year to see its length in days and weeks and the date the return is due, six months after the year-end as for any other year.

Any period, any lengthSix months is unchangedFlags a period over 53 weeksNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

The first and last day of the tax year

Enter both dates and the filing date appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Short Year Does Not Get a Short Deadline

The assumption worth correcting first: a shorter tax year does not come with a proportionally shorter filing window. Six months runs from the year-end whatever the length of the period behind it.

A two-month stub period and a twelve-month year both get six months from their year-end. The stub period does not get one month because it was one-sixth the length, and it does not get longer either.

Where Short Years Come From

Four situations produce one. A first tax year running from incorporation to the first year-end chosen. A change of fiscal year-end leaving a stub period at the changeover. A dissolution ending the year on its own date. An amalgamation ending a predecessor’s year the day before.

In all four the short period is a full tax year for filing purposes, needing its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year for a nil one.

The 53-Week Limit Applies to a First Year

A first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days counted from the date of incorporation to the year-end. A later tax year may run a full twelve months, so the limit only bites on a first year or on the first year of a corporation coming out of an amalgamation.

Where the period entered here is longer than 53 weeks and it is a first year, the year-end is probably not the one on record. The 53-week first tax year checker tests that question on its own.

Four Short Years, Four Filing Dates

Each row is a real short period of the kind that turns up, with its length and the date its return falls due. The six months is the same in every row.

Why the year is shortPeriodLengthReturn due
First year after incorporationMarch 12, 2026 to December 31, 2026295 daysJune 30, 2027
Stub period on a year-end changeJanuary 1, 2027 to March 31, 202790 daysSeptember 30, 2027
Final year on dissolutionApril 1, 2027 to August 20, 2027142 daysFebruary 22, 2028
Predecessor year on amalgamationJanuary 1, 2027 to June 30, 2027181 daysDecember 31, 2027

The dissolution row shows the shift at work, and it shows it twice. Six months after August 20, 2027 is February 20, 2028, a Sunday, so the date moves to the Monday — and that Monday is Family Day, so it moves again, to Tuesday February 22. The shift keeps stepping forward until it lands on a day that is open. The due date weekend and holiday shift calculator shows that step on its own.

Two year-ends in one calendar year means two returns, and each nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. A stub period is never folded into the year on either side of it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Short Year Filed Together With the Next Full Year?

No. It is a separate tax year and needs its own return. Two year-ends in one calendar year means two returns.

Does a Short Year Cost Less to File?

No. A nil return is $300.00 plus HST per tax year whatever the length of the period it covers.

Can a Tax Year Be Longer Than Twelve Months?

A first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days. Later years run to the fiscal year-end on record.

What Makes a Period a Stub Period?

A change of fiscal year-end leaves a gap between the old year-end and the new one. That gap is a tax year of its own.

Does the Filing Date Still Move for a Weekend?

Yes. The shift applies to a short year exactly as it does to a full one, so six months landing on a Saturday moves to the Monday.

title: Nil Return Late Penalty Checker | What Applies to a Late Nil Year
content:
Late Filing

Nil Return Late Penalty Checker

Three questions that set out what applies to a late nil T2: why the percentage penalty has nothing to apply to, and what still follows from leaving the year unfiled.

Three questionsThe full qualification, not a sloganSeparates resident from non-residentNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

Three questions about the year and the corporation

Answer all three and the position appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Why the Percentage Has Nothing to Apply To

The late-filing penalty on a T2 is a percentage of the tax owing. That is the mechanism, and it is the whole reason a nil year behaves differently from a year with a balance: a percentage of $0.00 is $0.00.

That is the first half of the position and not the whole of it. What follows is the whole of it, and the second half is the half that matters once a year has been sitting unfiled for a while.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

What an Unfiled Year Does Instead

The consequences of a late nil year are not financial at first. They are that the year stays open and keeps being a year that is open.

An open year invites a demand to file, and a demand opens the way to an arbitrary assessment, in which the Canada Revenue Agency assesses a figure of its own rather than waiting for the return. It blocks a clearance certificate, which blocks dissolution. None of that resolves itself with time.

The One Charge That Does Not Depend on Tax Owing

A non-resident-owned corporation is charged $25.00 per day for an unfiled return, up to $2,500.00. That charge runs on the lateness itself, so a nil year with no tax owing accrues it exactly as a year with a balance would, and it reaches its ceiling after 100 days.

The non-resident T2 penalty calculator works that figure out from the dates.

A Nil Year and a Year With Tax Owing, Side by Side

The difference is not in the form, the deadline or the fee. It is in whether there is a figure for a percentage to apply to.

What follows from filing lateA true nil yearA year with tax owing
Percentage late-filing penaltyNothing for the percentage to apply to, because the corporation owes $0.00Applies to the tax owing
The year stays openYesYes
Invites a demand to fileYesYes
Opens the way to an arbitrary assessmentYesYes
Blocks a clearance certificate and dissolutionYesYes
$25.00 per day up to $2,500.00 where non-resident-ownedYesYes
Cost of the return itself$300.00 plus HST per tax yearNot a nil return, so not this fee

Of the six rows describing what follows from filing late, five are identical down both columns. The percentage is the only consequence on which a nil year sits anywhere different, and it is the one people remember as though it were the whole list. The last row is not a consequence at all, it is the fee.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Late Nil Return Free of Consequences?

No. A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Does the Fee Go Up Because the Year Is Late?

No. A late nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, the same as one filed on time.

How Long Does the Non-Resident Charge Keep Running?

It accrues at $25.00 per day up to a ceiling of $2,500.00, which it reaches after 100 days.

What Changes Once a Demand to File Arrives?

The demand sets its own deadline, stated on the letter, and it opens the way to an arbitrary assessment. The guide to responding to a demand to file sets out what to do in what order.

What If the Year Turns Out Not to Have Been Nil?

Then the percentage has a figure to apply to and this is not the right tool. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

title: Clearance Certificate Requirement Checker | Before Assets Are Distributed
content:
Clearance

Clearance Certificate Requirement Checker

Three questions that set out whether a clearance certificate belongs in the plan and what has to be filed before one can be issued.

Three questionsNames the actual blockerCovers personal exposureNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

Three questions about the wind-down

Answer all three and the position appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What the Certificate Is For

A clearance certificate confirms the Canada Revenue Agency has no further claim against the corporation before its property is handed out. It is not a filing and it is not a tax return. It is a confirmation sought at the end, once everything that had to be filed has been.

Its purpose is personal rather than corporate. Distributing property without one leaves the person who distributed it exposed for amounts the corporation turns out to owe, and the corporation is by then gone or going.

An Unfiled Year Is the Usual Blocker

A certificate cannot be issued while a tax year is outstanding, because the position it is confirming is not yet known. That applies to nil years exactly as to any other: a year with nothing in it still has to be filed before it stops being outstanding.

The unfiled years checker lists which years are owed and the tax years since incorporation calculator lists every year the corporation has ever had. Each outstanding nil year is $300.00 plus HST per tax year, and several are transmitted in one sitting.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

The Order These Steps Fall In

Filing comes first, the certificate second, distribution third and dissolution last. Taken out of order the sequence stalls: a distribution made before the certificate cannot be undone by getting the certificate afterwards.

The dissolution readiness checker runs the full list, and the final T2 return due date calculator dates the last return.

Each Step, What It Needs First and What Goes Wrong Without It

The sequence only works in one direction. This is what each step depends on and what happens when it is taken early.

StepCannot happen untilTaken out of order
File every outstanding tax yearNothing. This is the first stepEverything after it stalls
File the final T2 for the period ending on dissolutionThe dissolution date is knownThe corporation has an unfiled final year
Request the clearance certificateEvery year, the final one included, is filedThe request cannot be granted while a year is outstanding
Distribute property to shareholdersThe certificate is issuedPersonal exposure for whatever the corporation turns out to owe
Complete the dissolutionThe property is distributedProperty is left in a corporation that no longer exists, and recovering it means reviving the corporation first

The second row is the one most often missed. The final T2 covers the period ending on the dissolution date, so it cannot be filed before that date is fixed, and the certificate cannot be requested before that return is in.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a Clearance Certificate Always Needed?

It belongs in any wind-down where property is being distributed, because that is the step it protects. With no distribution and no dissolution there is nothing for it to clear.

Do Nil Years Have to Be Filed First?

Yes. A nil year is an outstanding year until it is filed, and an outstanding year blocks the certificate.

Can Property Be Distributed First and Cleared Afterwards?

The exposure arises at the distribution, so a certificate obtained afterwards does not undo it. The order is the point.

How Many Returns Does a Dissolution Need?

Every unfiled earlier year, plus a final return for the short period ending on the dissolution date. Each nil one is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Does the Certificate Cover the Annual Return as Well?

No. The federal and Ontario annual returns go to a registry rather than to the Canada Revenue Agency and are separate from this. The inactive corporation filing checker sets out which filings go where.

title: Payroll Nil Remittance Checker | An Open Account With No Wages
content:
Payroll

Payroll Nil Remittance Checker

Three questions that set out whether an open payroll account still needs nil remittances, what the nil T2 does not cover and how the account is closed.

Three questionsOpen is not the same as dormantSays what the fee does not coverNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

Three questions about the payroll account

Answer all three and the payroll position appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Reporting Nothing Is Not the Same as Reporting Nil

An open payroll account expects to hear from the corporation on each of its due dates. Where no wages were paid, what it expects to hear is a nil remittance, and that is a positive statement rather than an absence of one.

Silence on an open account is what draws correspondence. The account has no way to tell the difference between a corporation that paid nothing and a corporation that paid something and did not report it, so it assumes the second.

The Nil T2 Does Not Touch It

Payroll and corporation income tax are separate programme accounts under one Business Number, each with its own filings. Filing the nil T2 settles the corporation income tax account for that tax year and does nothing at all about payroll.

The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the corporation income tax account only. The Business Number status checker sets out which accounts are open and what each one still needs.

Closing It Rather Than Keeping Up With It

Where the account is not going to be used again, the obligation ends by closing the account rather than by meeting it indefinitely. Form RC145 closes a Business Number programme account once that account has its own final remittance in.

An account left open can keep drawing correspondence after the corporation itself is gone, which is the usual reason a closed-down corporation keeps hearing from the Canada Revenue Agency.

Three Situations and What Each One Owes

The answers split three ways, and the middle one is the case most people are in and least expect.

SituationPayroll obligationEffect on the tax year
No payroll account on recordNothing to remit and nothing to closeNone. The year can still be nil
Account open, no wages paidA nil remittance on the account’s own cycle, for as long as it stays openNone. The year can still be nil
Account open, wages paidA real remittance of source deductions, not a nil oneWages are an expense, so the year is not nil

The third row has two consequences rather than one. The payroll remittance is real, and the tax year it falls in is not a nil year either, because paying wages is incurring an expense.

AccountWhat it carriesCovered by the fee here
Corporation income taxOne T2 for every tax year until the corporation is formally dissolvedYes
PayrollA remittance on its own cycle, nil ones included, until closed with Form RC145No
GST/HSTA return on its own cycle, nil ones included, until closed with Form RC145No

Frequently Asked Questions

Does an Open Payroll Account With No Employees Still Need Filing?

Yes. While the account is open it expects a remittance on its own cycle, and where no wages were paid that remittance is a nil one.

Does Filing the Nil T2 Cover the Payroll Account?

No. They are separate programme accounts. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the corporation income tax account only.

How Is a Payroll Account Closed?

With Form RC145, once the account has its own final remittance in.

Does Paying One Month of Wages Make the Year Not Nil?

Yes. Wages are an expense, so the tax year they fall in has a figure to report and is not a nil year.

What If the Account Was Opened and Never Used?

It is still open, so it still carries the obligation. Closing it with Form RC145 is what ends that.

title: GST/HST Account Closure Checker | Is the Account Ready for RC145
content:
GST/HST

GST/HST Account Closure Checker

Three questions that set out whether a GST/HST account is ready to close with Form RC145, what has to be filed first and what closing it does not do.

Three questionsNames what has to be filed firstSays what closing it does not doNo sign-up to use it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 27, 2026

Three questions about the GST/HST account

Answer all three and the closure position appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Final Return Comes Before the Closure

Form RC145 closes a Business Number programme account, but it does not clear what the account was already waiting for. The account has to have its own final return in first, and until then it stays open and keeps expecting a return on its own cycle, nil ones included.

That is the order, and taking it the other way round is the usual reason an account that was supposed to be closed is still sending letters.

Closing It Does Nothing About the T2

The corporation income tax account is a different programme account under the same Business Number. Closing GST/HST leaves it untouched, and a T2 is due for every tax year until the corporation is formally dissolved.

The GST/HST nil filing checker covers whether nil returns are owed on an open account, and the Business Number status checker sets out every account at once.

Still Trading Means It Is Not Ready

Where taxable sales are still being made the account is doing its job and closing it would be wrong. It also answers a different question: a corporation making sales has revenue, so the tax year those sales fall in is not a nil year.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Four States and What Each One Needs

The three answers produce four distinct positions, and only one of them is ready for Form RC145.

StateReady for Form RC145What is needed next
No GST/HST account on recordNothing to closeNothing on this account
Open, taxable sales still being madeNoKeep filing on the account’s own cycle. The tax year is not nil either
Open, no sales, returns outstandingNoFile the final return on the account, then close it
Open, no sales, final return filedYesForm RC145

In every one of these states the T2 position is unchanged. The corporation income tax account carries one return for every tax year until dissolution, and $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers that account only.

A Quebec corporation files a CO-17 as a separate return, and an Alberta corporation files an AT1 the same way. Neither is covered by the fee here, and neither is affected by closing a GST/HST account.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can the Account Be Closed With Returns Outstanding?

No. The account needs its own final return in first, and then Form RC145 closes it.

Does Closing GST/HST End the T2 Obligation?

No. They are separate programme accounts. A T2 is due for every tax year until the corporation is formally dissolved.

What If the Account Was Registered and Never Used?

It is still open, so it still expects a return on its own cycle. A nil return on the account, then Form RC145, is what ends that.

Is the GST/HST Return Covered by the Fee?

No. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers the corporation income tax account only. GST/HST is a separate filing.

Does Making Sales Affect the T2 as Well?

Yes. A corporation making taxable sales has revenue, so the tax year those sales fall in is not a nil year. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.
